inspection_scope: Read the complete texts and all sentence boundaries and roots for the nine remaining prepared Train states. Inspect selected token/head tables around the findings below. This does not inspect every token relationship in those documents. Earlier truncated tool output was reread in bounded complete-text views before counting an inspection.

findings.observed: A participial modifier of the subject becomes the root; the finite main predicate is its conjunct.
findings.expected: Attach the participial phrase to the subject and retain the finite main predicate as root.

findings.observed: A hyphenated verb prefix and its hyphen both receive VERB tags and conjunct dependencies.
findings.expected: The hyphen is punctuation, not another coordinated verb. Preserve the intended prefixed lexical verb.

findings.observed: The relative clause's object noun becomes its head, while the actual finite verb and noun modifier receive VERB compound analyses.
findings.expected: The finite verb heads the relative clause; its noun object and modifier retain their roles.

findings.observed: The phrase naming the code is attached to the programmers rather than to the code.
findings.expected: The naming parenthetical modifies the code. Proximity alone does not identify its antecedent.

findings.observed: The terminal period remains inside an abbreviation token and the following independent sentence is absorbed into the prior reporting clause.
findings.expected: Separate the two complete sentences and retain the second sentence's own subject and finite predicate.

findings.observed: An adjective selecting subregions becomes a verb coordinated with the reporting act; the embedded assertion loses its intended subject/predicate structure.
findings.expected: The selecting modifier belongs to the subregion noun phrase, within the reported assertion.

findings.observed: The subject noun becomes the root and its finite main predicate becomes an acl modifier.
findings.expected: Retain the finite main predicate and attach the noun phrase as its subject.

findings.observed: The subject publication name becomes the root; the main reporting predicate becomes an acl modifier after an appositive.
findings.expected: The finite reporting predicate heads the sentence, with the publication as subject and the naming explanation as apposition.

limitations: Four deliberately selected Train families do not estimate corpus accuracy or establish origin-specific error rates. Generated texts also contain substantive differences from their sources; this syntax review does not approve those revisions. Raw texts and full annotations remain outside the repository.
